correctness.rationale: Counting allowed edges after forbidding prescribed rows and columns gives every factorial moment. The overlap identity uv=rsN yields the positive finite product with factors 1-rsj/((N-rb-j)(N-as-j)), proving the strict sign for every positive marginal and at least two chosen edges; impossible joint events are handled separately. The balanced sparse constant follows from first-order log probability and second-order log ratio. Independent-edge and repeated-edge comparisons use direct independence; 58,896 exact-rational checks and 1,318 enumerated moment checks supplement the proof.

Priority uncertainty remains for older unindexed rectangular occupancy literature.

value.rationale: Isolated vertices are natural obstructions to bipartite connectivity and perfect matching. At equal expected edge count, the sign of cross-part isolation covariance switches from negative for distinct fixed-edge sampling, to zero for repeated independent edge draws, to positive for Bernoulli edges. Strict negativity holds for every positive cross-part factorial moment, and its balanced sparse covariance has a nonzero order-one limit despite a much larger Bernoulli covariance. This exact mechanism distinguishes ensembles beyond standard leading-order occupancy approximations.
